bullets: Training as a Python backend engineer at an AI-native development agency, building a REST-API foundation with FastAPI, PostgreSQL and the UV package manager on top of core web internals (HTTP/HTTPS, DNS, reverse proxies, Nginx).

Caching, proven with load tests — added a Redis cache to an API's list endpoint and measured it with a Locust before/after load-test harness: peak throughput +39% (207 → 287 req/s), tail latency under load down from 920 ms to 200 ms (p95), and database CPU dropped to ~10%.

Choosing the right message broker for the job — designed a fleet-telemetry system as event-driven microservices and chose Apache Kafka over RabbitMQ: a high-volume, replayable stream of vehicle readings that several services consume independently fits Kafka's partitioned, durable log, where RabbitMQ suits one-off task queues. Used the transactional outbox pattern so no event is lost or double-sent across restarts.

A real test suite and CI/CD pipeline, not mocks — integration tests run against a throwaway PostgreSQL spun up in Docker with testcontainers (against the real database migrations), and a GitHub Actions pipeline runs Ruff lint/format checks plus the full test suite on every push and pull request.

Building fundamentals independently — solving a LeetCode problem in Python every day and committing each as a documented Jupyter notebook (~25 this past month), reasoning through the data-structure and complexity trade-offs myself, with no AI assistance.

Completing Anthropic's official curriculum (Claude Code, Agent Skills, MCP), including custom Python MCP servers that connect Claude to PostgreSQL and local APIs — ahead of moving onto real client projects.
